gaps.sentence: I ___ exactly what you mean, so there is no need to explain again.
gaps.explanation: 'Understand' is a state verb and is not used in continuous forms, so the present simple is correct.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her grandmother every Sunday; it is a promise she never breaks.
gaps.hint: every Sunday marks repeated routine action
gaps.explanation: 'Every Sunday' signals a regularly repeated action, so the present simple is correct: visits.

gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: What ___ at eleven o'clock last night? I called you twice.
gaps.hint: at eleven o'clock means a point in past
gaps.explanation: A specific past moment asks about an action in progress then, so the past continuous fits: were you doing.

gaps.sentence: This is the best pizza I ___ in years.
gaps.hint: superlative experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Superlative statements about experience up to now take the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: I ___ this temperature to the heat.
gaps.explanation: 'Prefer' is a state verb and takes the present simple: prefer.

gaps.sentence: Shakespeare ___ thirty-seven plays that we know of.
gaps.hint: a dead historical figure, finished lifetime
gaps.explanation: Actions of people who are no longer alive take the past simple even without a time phrase: wrote.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, with my phone switched off.
gaps.hint: this time next week means in progress
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous fits: will be lying.
